Reproducible preprocessing pipelines

glyclean_pipeline.Rd

Build an unevaluated sequence of glyclean processing calls, apply it to one experiment, or retrieve the processing history of an experiment.

Usage

glyclean_pipeline(...)

get_pipeline(exp)

apply_pipeline(exp, pipeline)

Arguments

...

Calls to glyclean processing functions. Omit the experiment and name every argument explicitly; positional and partially matched arguments are not accepted. Parameter expressions are evaluated once when building the pipeline, including default values, but processing functions are not run. Calls and parameter expressions support tidy-evaluation injection with !! and !!!.

exp

A supported glyclean experiment.

pipeline

A glyclean_pipeline list.

Value

glyclean_pipeline() and get_pipeline() return a glyclean_pipeline list. apply_pipeline() returns a processed experiment.

Details

A pipeline is a list of glyclean_step lists. Each step has exactly two fields: function (the function object) and parameters (a named list). Use step[["function"]] to inspect the function. Pipelines are ordinary lists, not callable functions: use apply_pipeline(exp, pipeline).

Successful processing calls append to metadata(exp)$pipeline (or exp$meta_data$pipeline for legacy experiments). Automatic operations record the concrete operations they execute. QC summaries and plots do not modify history. The experiment still contains only one abundance assay; history contains parameters, not copies of intermediate assays. Grouping values are frozen for replay. When by is supplied as a column name, that original name is retained for printing the recorded step.

Replaying a history requires the same original input and compatible package versions and RNG configuration. Each stochastic operation records its explicit seed in parameters, including the default when omitted. Replay passes these parameters directly to the operation. Steps carry package-version information as an attribute; no random-generator state is stored. Callback functions and parameter values are captured at construction/recording time; external files, network side effects and mutable references in arbitrary callbacks are not supported. Site-sequence annotation records the actual sequences.

Examples

pipeline <- glyclean_pipeline(normalize_total_area(), impute_min_prob(seed = 42))
cleaned <- apply_pipeline(glyexp::real_experiment, pipeline)
history <- get_pipeline(cleaned)
